LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Active Listening

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Active Listening. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the strategies of active listening?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information
2. describe animals based on their size and colour

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ACTIVE LISTENING
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Active Listening helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ACTIVE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe animals based on their size and colour

What this means
In this part you learn to describe animals based on their size and colour. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe animals based on their size and colour.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe animals based on their size and colour. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Active Listening is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening to a partner. (skill: describe animals based on their size and colour)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Active Listening to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information.
3. Practise this skill: describe animals based on their size and colour.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Active Listening from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Active Listening: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Active Listening?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the strategies of active listening?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Active Listening means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify animals (pets, farm, and wild animals) for information.
5. Be able to: describe animals based on their size and colour.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
